description: Tabulated u(y) along the vertical centerline (x=0.5) and v(x) along the horizontal centerline (y=0.5) for the 2-D lid-driven cavity at several Reynolds numbers. Coordinates and velocities are non-dimensional: cavity side = 1, lid velocity U_lid = 1. The reference points are sampled at the non-uniform y and x stations used by Ghia, Ghia, & Shin (1982) Tables I and II.

convention.reynolds_number: Re = U_lid * L / nu, where L is the cavity side length and U_lid is the moving-lid velocity
convention.geometry: Square cavity. Top wall (y=1) moves at U_lid in the +x direction; the other three walls are no-slip. 2-D, incompressible, steady.
convention.non_dimensionalization: All velocities normalized by U_lid; all coordinates normalized by L.

ghia_re_100_u_centerline.description: u-velocity along the vertical line x=0.5 at Re=100. Ghia Table I, leftmost data column.

ghia_re_100_v_centerline.description: v-velocity along the horizontal line y=0.5 at Re=100. Ghia Table II, leftmost data column.

ghia_re_400_u_centerline.description: u-velocity along the vertical line x=0.5 at Re=400. Ghia Table I, second data column.

ghia_re_400_v_centerline.description: v-velocity along the horizontal line y=0.5 at Re=400. Ghia Table II, second data column.

ghia_re_1000_u_centerline.description: u-velocity along the vertical line x=0.5 at Re=1000. Ghia Table I, third data column.

ghia_re_1000_v_centerline.description: v-velocity along the horizontal line y=0.5 at Re=1000. Ghia Table II, third data column. No suspected typo at x=0.9063 (v=-0.51500 is the smooth trough); the typo flag applies only to the Re=400 column.

tolerance.rationale: 5% relative-L2 error against Ghia is a standard acceptance threshold for benchmark cavity studies. The grid resolution that meets it is NOT known in advance and must not be assumed: establish it by refining the mesh until the centerline profiles stop changing and converge toward this reference (a grid-convergence / mesh-independence study), not by picking a cell count up front. The only sourced grid anchor is Ghia, Ghia & Shin's own solution, computed on a 129x129 uniform mesh; a converged 2nd-order solver should approach the 5% band as the grid is refined toward that resolution. The threshold catches mesh under-resolution while letting a converged 2nd-order solution pass. Do not cite a specific cell count as a known-good resolution — there is no published source for one, and demonstrating the convergence is the point.

primary_citation: Ghia, U., Ghia, K. N., & Shin, C. T. (1982). High-Re solutions for incompressible flow using the Navier-Stokes equations and a multigrid method. Journal of Computational Physics, 48(3), 387-411.
data_provenance: Hand-encoded from reproductions of Ghia's Tables I and II that circulate in the cavity-benchmark community. Verified on 2026-05-21 against a publicly mirrored transcription of Ghia's Tables I and II (gist.github.com/ivan-pi/3e9326d18a366ffe6a8e5bfda6353219 for Table I u; gist.github.com/ivan-pi/caa6c6737d36a9140fbcf2ea59c78b3c for Table II v). All shipped values match Ghia's printed table to 5 decimal places across the six datasets (Re=100, Re=400, and Re=1000, u and v each). KNOWN SUSPECTED TYPO, SHIPPED AS-PRINTED: in `ghia_re_400_v_centerline` at x=0.9063, Ghia's Table II prints v=-0.23827, which the transcription source annotates as 'probably wrong' (it is an outlier in an otherwise smooth v(x) profile, sitting between -0.44993 at x=0.8594 and -0.22847 at x=0.9453). We ship Ghia's printed value -0.23827 unchanged rather than substitute an unsourced replacement: no published benchmark re-tabulates Re=400 v-centerline data (Botella & Peyret 1998 Comput. Fluids 27 is Re=1000 only; Erturk, Corke & Gokcol 2005 Int. J. Numer. Methods Fluids 48 tabulates Re=1000-21000 only), so none can adjudicate the suspected typo. Do NOT substitute the smoothed value -0.33827 that circulates in some transcriptions: it is unsourced for Re=400. Re=100, Re=400, and Re=1000 columns are encoded (Re=1000 added and verified 2026-05-28 against the same two mirror gists, whose Table II header itself carries the 'probably wrong' note on the Re=400 x=0.9063 point); Re>=3200 columns from Ghia's tables are not included. The Re=1000 v-centerline carries NO suspected typo — its x=0.9063 value -0.51500 is the smooth trough — so the typo caveat above is specific to the Re=400 column.
units: All non-dimensional: u, v normalized by U_lid; x, y normalized by L.
